Package org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.scripting.engine

Class GraalJsNumberNarrowing

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.scripting.engine.GraalJsNumberNarrowing
public final class GraalJsNumberNarrowing extends Object
Keeps the Java type of the numbers that JavaScript scripts on GraalJS hand to Java as CIB seven 2.2 did.

Since GraalJS 24, a Java long stays a long inside JavaScript, and arithmetic with it gives a double. A script that passes execution.getVariable('count'), java.lang.Long.valueOf(7) or the count of a query to execution.setVariable therefore stores a Long variable, where GraalJS 21 (CIB seven 2.2) stored an Integer. This class builds the polyglot HostAccess of the GraalJS contexts of the process engine: HostAccess.ALL with a target type mapping that turns such a number into an Integer when a script hands it to a Java parameter of type Object (such as setVariable(String, Object)) or returns it as its result. The modes:

  • LONG (the default): a Java long in int range becomes an Integer. A double stays a Double, also the result of arithmetic with a long (lng + 1 gives 6.0).
  • NONE: the types GraalJS gives (Long, Double).
The mapping has the precedence LOW: of a Java method overloaded for int and Object, such as List.remove, the same one is chosen as without the mapping.

All contexts of one polyglot engine must use the same host access. A narrowed script engine that a script engine factory would create therefore runs on a polyglot engine of this class, one per factory and host access (with and without the Nashorn compatibility mode), and never on the polyglot engine of the factory: script engines without narrowing use that one with HostAccess.ALL, for example those of a process application that two process engines with different modes share. CamundaScriptEngineManager (useCibSevenNamespaceInScripting) gives each script engine a polyglot engine of its own, and takes only the host access from this class. GraalJS is used through reflection: the process engine has no compile dependency on it.

In the Nashorn compatibility mode (enableScriptEngineNashornCompatibility), the host access is the one GraalJS uses in that mode (with the conversions of Nashorn) with the same mapping, and the context gets the settings GraalJS gives it in that mode. The system property polyglot.js.nashorn-compat gives a script engine of the factory these settings too, as GraalJS does; unlike GraalJS, which reads it once when its class is loaded, this class reads it at each script engine it creates.
